The stochastic greedy-dispatch counterexample is unrelated. The cycle-packing routine is used only with a static maximality certificate for approximation, while the chain-graph routine evaluates an exhaustive candidate family exactly.

The parent already guards against the non-maximal-packing error: it scans the complete short-cycle list and adds every cycle disjoint from the current packing, so any cycle disjoint from the final union contradicts its scan decision.

The omitted-case warning does not change the proof. The cycle argument covers every even length as 4, 6, 8, or at least 10, and the strengthened obstruction statements explicitly cover n≥2 (and separately test their smallest cases).

The invalid exponent-induction example is unrelated. No exponent induction is used; runtime exponents arise from direct enumeration and bounded search-tree arity and depth.

The functional-equation arithmetic error is unrelated; no recurrence of that kind appears, and all new numerical formulas use exact integer or Fraction checks.

results.claim: Short-obstruction equivalence and radius-three normal form: in a P8-free bipartite graph, a set S is a feedback vertex set exactly when it meets every induced C4, C6, and C8. Moreover, every component of G-S has radius at most 3; if S is inclusion-minimal, every x in S has two neighbors in one component of G-S.
results.proof_sketch: If G-S contains a cycle, choose a shortest one. It is chordless, hence induced in G. Bipartiteness makes its length even. An induced cycle of length at least 10 contains an induced P8 on eight consecutive vertices, impossible; thus the cycle is C4, C6, or C8. The converse is immediate, so hitting those induced cycles is equivalent to being an FVS. Once S is an FVS, every component of G-S is a tree. A tree of diameter at least 7 contains an induced eight-vertex path, so its diameter is at most 6 and its radius at most 3. If S is inclusion-minimal and x∈S, then G-(S minus {x}) has a cycle. Since G-S is a forest, that cycle uses x, and deleting x from it leaves a path in one component of G-S between two distinct neighbors of x.

results.claim: There is an exact parameterized algorithm running in O(8^k n^8) time for solutions of size at most k, as well as a polynomial-time 8-approximation.
results.proof_sketch: Enumerate all vertex subsets of sizes 4, 6, and 8 and retain those whose induced graph is exactly a cycle. By the preceding equivalence, the resulting rank-at-most-eight hypergraph has exactly the feedback vertex sets as its transversals. For the decision problem, select an unhit hyperedge and branch on deleting each of its at most eight vertices, giving O(8^k n^8) time and exhaustive coverage. For approximation, greedily construct a maximal family of vertex-disjoint listed cycles and return their union U. Maximality makes U a transversal and hence an FVS. If the family has p cycles, every FVS contains at least one vertex from each, so OPT≥p, while |U|≤8p≤8OPT.

results.claim: Every C4-free P8-free bipartite graph has treewidth at most 13. Consequently, Feedback Vertex Set is polynomial-time solvable on this subclass.
results.proof_sketch: An exact finite enumeration gives the following lemma: no C4-free P8-free bipartite graph contains a simple path on 15 vertices. Fixing a required path's vertex order forces every allowable chord to join opposite index parities. Introducing vertices in order and rejecting exactly those extensions that create a C4 or an induced P8 gives survivor counts 1,1,1,1,1,2,3,5,7,10,10,11,6,3,0 for orders 1 through 15. Any hypothetical 15-vertex path would induce one of these exhaustively considered ordered graphs. Now run an undirected DFS forest. Every edge has ancestor-comparable endpoints, and each root-to-leaf path has at most 14 vertices. For each DFS vertex, the bag consisting of it and all its ancestors yields a tree decomposition: an edge shares the descendant endpoint's bag, and bags containing a fixed vertex form its descendant subtree. Thus the width is at most 13. A fixed-width forest-connectivity dynamic program computes minimum FVS in polynomial time.

results.claim: More generally, Feedback Vertex Set is fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the minimum number r of vertices meeting every C4; a concrete bound is 4^r·2^{O(r log r)}·n^{O(1)}.
results.proof_sketch: Within P8-free bipartite graphs, iterative deepening branches on the four vertices of an uncovered induced C4; at depth r it finds a minimum C4-transversal X in O(4^r n^{O(1)}) time. Then G-X is C4-free and remains P8-free and bipartite, so the previous claim gives a constructible width-13 decomposition. Add X to every bag, obtaining width at most r+13. On a nice decomposition, record the deleted bag vertices and the connectivity partition induced by retained partial-forest vertices; introduce-edge and join transitions reject precisely combinations that close a cycle. There are 2^{O(r log r)} states per bag. Minimizing deletion cost therefore computes an exact FVS within the claimed total bound.

results.claim: On a chain graph—one whose neighborhoods on a bipartition side are linearly ordered by inclusion—a maximum-gain induced forest for arbitrary rational vertex gains, with one specified vertex optionally forced retained or deleted, is constructible in O(n^2). Consequently, weighted Feedback Vertex Set is polynomial-time solvable on chain graphs, including half-graphs with unbounded C4-transversal number.
results.proof_sketch: Let A={a_1,...,a_p}, B={b_1,...,b_m}. Sort A by decreasing nested neighborhoods, then B by nonincreasing last A-neighbor, obtaining N(a_i)={b_1,...,b_{d_i}} and d_1≥...≥d_p. For retained A',B', the induced graph is a forest iff at most one retained A-vertex has two retained B-neighbors: a cycle violates this, while two such A-vertices have two common neighbors by nesting and form a C4. Write z^+=max(z,0), with empty maxima contributing 0. For gains w and |B'|≤1, the optimum is Σ_i w(a_i)^+ + max(0,max_j w(b_j)). Otherwise let q be the second selected B-position. The optimum among sets with this q is max_{j<q}w(b_j)+w(b_q)+Σ_{j>q}w(b_j)^+ +Σ_{d_i<q}w(a_i)^+ +max(0,max_{d_i≥q}w(a_i)). Indeed, exactly one earlier B-vertex and b_q are mandatory; later B-vertices and low A-vertices are independent choices; at most one high A-vertex is allowed. The displayed choices attain the bound. Evaluate all q=2,...,m. To force deletion, remove the vertex and reorder. To force retention, add a bonus M>2Σ_v|w(v)| to its gain, optimize, and subtract M; every boosted optimum then retains it. For nonnegative deletion costs, maximizing retained cost is weighted FVS. Nested neighborhoods forbid induced 2K2, whereas P5 contains one, so chain graphs are P5-free and lie in the target class.

results.claim: Feedback Vertex Set is polynomial-time solvable on graphs whose every block is a chain graph. This gives a direct exact algorithm for a P8-free subclass that can contain both C4 and an induced P7.
results.proof_sketch: Every cycle lies wholly in one block, so a retained vertex set is a forest exactly when its intersection with every original block induces a forest. The block-cut incidence graph is a forest. Root each component and pass two-value messages, indexed by whether the shared articulation vertex is deleted or retained. At a block node, incoming messages from its other articulation vertices and the original vertex costs become arbitrary unary gains on that block. Conditional on the parent articulation's state, the required block-to-parent message is exactly the maximum-gain induced-forest problem on a chain graph with that one vertex forced; the preceding construction computes it in polynomial time. Non-articulation vertices occur in only one block, and assigning each articulation's original cost once prevents double counting. Bottom-up combination therefore gives the global optimum. This subclass genuinely reaches the stated boundary: on C4=a_1b_1a_2b_2a_1 attach pendant paths a_1x_1x_2 and a_2y_1y_2. The graph has eight vertices and is not itself P8, while x_2x_1a_1b_1a_2y_1y_2 is an induced P7. Its blocks are K_{2,2} and four bridges, all chain graphs.

results.claim: For every n≥2, the half-graph H_n is P5-free and has no false twins, yet its minimum C4-transversal has size n-2 and its treewidth is at least ⌈n/2⌉. Thus neither bounded C4-transversal number nor bounded treewidth follows from P8-freeness, even after excluding false twins.
results.proof_sketch: Let A={a_1,...,a_n}, B={b_1,...,b_n}, with a_i b_j iff i≤j. The neighborhoods are strictly nested within each side and nonempty subsets of opposite sides across the bipartition, so no two vertices are false twins. Nested neighborhoods forbid an induced 2K2; since every P5 contains an induced 2K2 on its first two and last two vertices, H_n is P5-free. If a retained C4-free set contains at least two A-vertices, let a_j be its second-lowest-index one. It retains at most n-j+2 A-vertices and at most j B-vertices, hence at most n+2 vertices; the cases with fewer than two A-vertices are no larger. Keeping all B together with a_{n-1},a_n attains n+2, so the transversal number is 2n-(n+2)=n-2. Put p=⌈n/2⌉. The vertices a_1,...,a_p and b_p,...,b_n induce a K_{p,n-p+1}, containing K_{p,p}. Contract p-1 disjoint edges of K_{p,p}; the resulting branch sets plus the two unmatched endpoints form a K_{p+1} minor. Treewidth is minor-monotone and tw(K_{p+1})=p, so tw(H_n)≥p.

results.claim: There are 2-connected C4-free P8-free bipartite graphs of unbounded order: the graph formed by m≥2 internally disjoint length-three paths between two common terminals has 2m+2 vertices.
results.proof_sketch: Write the m arms as u-x_i-y_i-v. Every cycle uses exactly two arms, so every cycle has length six and the graph is C4-free. Deleting u or v leaves a connected subdivided star centered at the other terminal; deleting an internal vertex leaves its remaining arm piece attached to one terminal, while another intact arm still joins the terminals. Thus there is no cut vertex for m≥2. For induced paths, after deleting u and v the arms are disjoint edges. A path using neither terminal has at most two vertices; one using exactly one terminal has at most five; and one using both can use one full arm between them and at most one additional internal vertex beyond each terminal, for at most six vertices. Hence the graph is P8-free. Its order 2m+2 is unbounded, ruling out any bounded-block-order route even on the C4-free side.

results.claim: The natural LP that assigns nonnegative vertex weights and requires total weight at least one on every induced C4, C6, and C8 has integrality gap at least 2-o(1) on P8-free bipartite graphs: on K_{n,n} its exact fractional optimum is n/2 while its FVS optimum is n-1.
results.proof_sketch: K_{n,n} is P4-free: four alternating vertices of a putative induced P4 acquire the endpoint chord. Its only induced cycles are C4s. A retained induced subgraph is a forest exactly when one bipartition side has at most one retained vertex, so at most n+1 vertices can remain, and this is attainable; hence OPT_FVS=n-1. There are binom(n,2)^2 induced C4s, and every vertex occurs in (n-1)binom(n,2) of them. Summing all C4 inequalities gives (n-1)binom(n,2)·Σ_v x_v≥binom(n,2)^2, hence Σ_v x_v≥n/2. Equality is attained by x_v=1/4 for every vertex. Therefore the exact gap is (n-1)/(n/2)=2-2/n, which tends to 2. The boundary n=2 has gap 1, and n=3 recovers the parent's K_{3,3} values 2 versus 3/2.

final_writeup:
The target asks for a polynomial-time algorithm for Feedback Vertex Set on all P8-free bipartite graphs. I do not establish that target, so the resolution remains PARTIAL. The obstruction-first attempt does strengthen the known boundaries quantitatively while preserving the audited structural and algorithmic progress.

Let G be P8-free and bipartite. A set S is an FVS exactly when it meets every induced C4, C6, and C8. If G-S has a cycle, a shortest one is chordless and hence induced in G. Its length is even; length at least 10 would make eight consecutive vertices an induced P8. Conversely, an FVS meets every cycle. Each component of G-S is therefore a tree of diameter at most 6 and radius at most 3. If S is inclusion-minimal, restoring any x∈S creates a cycle through x, whose remainder joins two neighbors of x inside one component of G-S.

This is an exact rank-eight hitting-set formulation. Enumerating the short induced cycles and branching on an uncovered one gives an O(8^k n^8) decision algorithm for solutions of size k. The union of a maximal vertex-disjoint packing of listed cycles is an 8-approximation: maximality makes it a transversal, while p disjoint cycles require at least p deleted vertices and contribute at most 8p vertices to the union.

There is a polynomial boundary at C4-freeness. Exact finite enumeration shows that no C4-free P8-free bipartite graph contains a 15-vertex simple path. In a DFS forest, every edge has ancestor-comparable endpoints and every root-to-leaf path consequently has at most 14 vertices. The bags consisting of a DFS vertex and all its ancestors form a tree decomposition of width at most 13. Fixed-width connectivity dynamic programming solves FVS on this subclass. If r is the minimum C4-transversal size, branching finds a transversal X in O(4^r n^{O(1)}) time; adding X to every bag of a width-13 decomposition of G-X gives width at most r+13. Partition-based FVS dynamic programming then yields 4^r·2^{O(r log r)}·n^{O(1)} time.

A different polynomial island handles dense C4 structure. In a chain graph, choose Ferrers order N(a_i)={b_1,...,b_{d_i}}. A retained induced subgraph is a forest exactly when at most one retained A-vertex has two retained B-neighbors: a cycle forces two, while two have two common retained neighbors and form a C4. Conditioning on the second retained B-position makes all later B choices and low-degree A choices independent and permits at most one high-degree A choice. Enumerating these cases optimizes arbitrary signed vertex gain in O(n^2), including one forced retained or deleted vertex, and therefore solves weighted FVS on chain graphs. Two-state messages at articulation vertices compose this oracle over the block-cut forest, giving a polynomial algorithm whenever every block is a chain graph. This P8-free subclass can contain both a C4 and an induced P7.

The required obstruction lens shows why none of these arguments automatically extends. First, the half-graph H_n, with a_i adjacent to b_j exactly when i≤j, is already P5-free and has no false twins. Its maximum C4-free retained set has n+2 vertices, so its minimum C4-transversal is n-2. More strongly, with p=⌈n/2⌉ it contains K_{p,p} as a subgraph and hence a K_{p+1} minor, giving treewidth at least p. Thus P8-freeness plus false-twin reduction bounds neither the C4-transversal parameter nor treewidth.

Second, m internally disjoint length-three paths between two terminals form a 2-connected, C4-free, P8-free graph on 2m+2 vertices. Every cycle uses two arms and has length six, while an induced path has at most six vertices. Hence even C4-free 2-connected blocks have unbounded order.

Third, the short-cycle covering LP has a quantitative barrier. K_{n,n} is P4-free and has only induced C4s. Its FVS optimum is n-1, because a forest can retain at most one vertex on one side and therefore at most n+1 vertices total. The LP has exact optimum n/2: uniform weight 1/4 is feasible, and summing all binom(n,2)^2 C4 constraints gives the matching lower bound. Its integrality gap is therefore 2-2/n, tending to 2. This strengthens the isolated K_{3,3} nonintegrality witness but is not a hardness result.

These are precise limitations only. The general exact algorithm is exponential in k, the bounded-treewidth algorithm assumes C4-freeness, r is unbounded, and the chain-block algorithm assumes nested neighborhoods inside every block. Unbounded treewidth and an LP gap do not preclude a different decomposition or a different polynomial algorithm. No polynomial-time algorithm for the whole target class is proved here.
